newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sends ministers back to school.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sends ministers back to school.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday sent his top ministers back to school and told pupils not to be afraid to ask them questions.

Yeltsin, speaking in a radio address, said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, ministers, local governors and city mayors should give lessons in local schools to explain the history of the new Russia.

"I would particularly like to address the schoolchildren," he said. "Do not be afraid of your superiors and ask them the most pointed questions, you have every right to do this. Write to me and tell me how the lesson went. You are our future."
Yeltsin, who is being prepared for open heart surgery in the exclusive Central Clinical Hospital, targeted the youth vote during the presidential election campaign.
His campaign team sent personalised letters to all new voters before the first round and to those turning 18 between the two rounds of the election.
He won the runoff convincingly against communist Gennady Zyuganov but disappeared from public view before the vote.
On September 5 he admitted he needed an operation on his heart and went into hospital eight days later. Doctors say it will take 6-10 weeks to prepare him for surgery.
